column4: Cold iced tea running from the small plastic push tap of an orange drinks cooler barrel into a thin plastic cup, filling it, outdoors at a roadside stand. Close up, no music, no voices.
A small clear plastic bag full of lemonade twisted shut round a bendy drinking straw and knotted: crinkling plastic, a short squeak. Close up, outdoors, no music, no voices.

The heavy chrome side lever of an old 1970s mechanical one-armed-bandit slot machine pulled down and released: a metal ratchet clunk and a spring snapping back. Close up, small village pub, no music, no voices.
The three mechanical reels of an old one-armed-bandit slot machine spinning: a fast whirring clatter of gears inside a metal cabinet. Close up, small pub, no music, no voices.
One mechanical reel of an old slot machine stopping with a single sharp clack. Close up, no music, no voices.
A small win on an old mechanical slot machine: a little bell rings twice and a handful of coins clatter down into its metal payout tray. Close up, village pub, no music, no voices.
A steel-tipped dart thrown and hitting a sisal dartboard on a wooden wall: a short whoosh and a dull thock. Small pub, no music, no voices.
A short stroke of a carpenter's pencil on a cardboard beer mat lying on a wooden bar: a quick dry scratch. Close up, no music, no voices.
One old worn playing card dealt and flipped onto a wooden pub table: a soft slap and slide. Close up, no music, no voices.

A gold crown cap levered off a cold half-litre glass soda bottle with a steel bottle opener: a sharp pop and a short fizzing hiss, the little metal cap pinging off onto a laminate counter. Close up, canteen, no music, no voices.
A thick sausage turned over on a hot cast-iron grill grate with steel tongs: a click of the tongs and a fresh loud sizzle. Close up, kitchen, no music, no voices.
A long sharp knife cutting one thin slice off a hard salami stick on a wooden board: a short firm slicing sound and a tap on the board. Close up, small grocery, no music, no voices.
Something set down on the steel plate of an old mechanical shop scale: a soft clank and the needle springing round, settling with a little rattle. Close up, small grocery, no music, no voices.
A few slices of salami wrapped in stiff grey grocer's paper: the paper torn off the roll, folded and creased with quick crinkling. Close up, no music, no voices.
